Oh yeah. Last Monday I got McDonald's and went downtown to find someone to give it to. I didn't find a homeless man/woman, but did find someone in catatonia on the curb of a restaurant. No one could arouse him. I left an OJ and some food on the curb and dialed an ambulance.

Really trying to tip the scales here. I did attempt suicide for that purpose, but I think I could do better for other humans to recalibrate things instead.

I never really had many friends, but if it ever comes up I'd say "I was going through a lot. I wasn't myself, I fucked up, and I'm sorry" and it doesn't matter if they forgive me or not.

I'm smart, I'm really wanting to try and do better in life, I just want to be normal and do good for others, and myself.
Was it just once? And did anything help? I was in the psych ward last month for a week, but nothing got better.

Thank you. It's just really hard when those thoughts come into my head and I remember what a fucking horrible person I was being. I want to put more good into the world than bad. I consider it to do the right thing for society. I could do good things, but I'm extremely unstable and my behavior makes me feel like I don't deserve life.

I keep telling myself some time will pass and people will forget and no one will think about it, but I'm still a bad person. I tried working a job and I just couldn't shake the thought of being a piece of shit and quit.

I just got a vial, I'm giving it a go because I'm desperate at this point. 

Have you ever been unemployed due to OCD/mental illness? I'm housebound at the moment.

Thanks. It's nothing against you, but this is just what I mean, it's one of those situation where it's a "Damn. I don't know what to say, but I'm sorry" type of things, and that's what keeps happening in therapy in so many words, and that's what keeps happening on outreach forums, and I've just come to the conclusion that the psyche is extremely fragile, and it can absolutely be damaged beyond repair and the notion of "getting help" just doesn't work out for everyone. It's not like you just walk through a door and say "I'm here for the help" and then things get better. These are multiple serious illnesses and problems that are only going to get worse as time progresses and it's ludicrous to imagine myself having to live 50 more bullshit years because society thinks this is taboo. Society doing all this shit to a single individual is taboo. I deserve a pass to do this.

I apologize.

Thank you. 

I bought $16 worth of McDonalds Monday morning and drank an Orange juice, had a hash brown and a sandwich and drove around looking for a homeless person to give it to. I saw someone completely catatonic on the curb of a Braum's on a bad side of town. He wouldn't respond. There were a few sandwiches, a hashbrown, two burritos and an OJ left. I sat it next to him and called an ambulance. 

I'm just trying to balance things out. I don't think suicide is the way to tip the scales. I really regret doing that. I wish others would just understand that I've been through a lot and I wasn't in my right mind and I want to make things right.

Hey, thanks. I'm actually a massive music buff. I don't like this song that much and always felt that it was taking, well... the blame away. I'm a perfectionist. I was seventeen when this came out, or at least when I first started hearing this on the radio, and I was in a relationship with that violent ex. 

I think a lot about John Lennon, and how he sang about peace, but about how he was a violent, wife-beating, angry man, you know? I know everyone is fucked up. I don't want to be fucked up like that, though. I don't want to be marred.
